# Symphony + Claude Lane

> An installable agent skill that adds Claude Code workers alongside Codex in OpenAI Symphony + Linear workflows. Symphony dispatches Codex workers through its Elixir runtime; this skill adds Claude workers via `claude -p`, tracked through the same Linear backlog, with smart routing that sends each task to the right agent.

## What this is

A skill you install into an AI coding agent (Codex or Claude Code) that teaches the orchestrator how to run Claude workers alongside Symphony's Codex workers. Once installed, your agent can analyze each issue's characteristics, pick the best model, launch Claude workers securely in isolated git worktrees, create a durable routing profile, and define visual verification, privacy, and closeout rules. Also supports Claude-only setups without Codex. No API plumbing required — both Codex and Claude Code are subscription tools with built-in agent capabilities.

## Who this is for

Developers and operators who run Symphony + Linear with Codex workers and want to add Claude Code for tasks that benefit from visual judgment, deep reasoning, browser verification, external tool access, security review, or documentation quality. Also for teams that want Claude-only workers against Linear issues without Codex.

## How the two runtimes work together

Symphony (Elixir) dispatches Codex workers — managing worktrees, scheduling, and process supervision. Claude workers run via `claude -p` directly — launched by the orchestrator or a launcher script, not through Symphony's runtime. Linear is the shared control plane for both: issues, state transitions, routing labels, and closeout all live there regardless of which agent executes the work.

## Key concepts

- **Task-Characteristic Routing**: The orchestrator analyzes each issue and picks the best model based on what the task requires. Labels serve as overrides.
- **Label-Only Routing**: Alternative strategy where routing is determined entirely by Linear labels. Simpler but less adaptive.
- **Claude-Only Mode**: For teams without Codex. All tasks route to Claude. The dispatch contract still applies.
- **Routing Profile**: A repo-local YAML file (`.orchestration/claude-lane.yaml`) that records model selection criteria, label overrides, privacy rules, guardrails, and cleanup policy.
- **Visual Verification**: Playwright-first browser verification for tickets affecting rendered output.

## When to prefer Claude

- Requires browser verification or visual judgment
- Requires deep reasoning (architecture, complex debugging)
- Requires external tools (MCP servers, APIs, databases)
- Involves security review, code review, or documentation
- Involves product copy or technical writing
- Breaks in Codex sandbox (E2E tests, integration tests)

## When to prefer Codex

- Bounded implementation with clear acceptance criteria
- Sandbox-compatible (no network, browser, or system access needed)
- Parallelizable batch of similar tasks
- Config, schema, type, or migration changes
- Test infrastructure or mechanical refactors

## Default workflow

Inspect repo -> confirm multi-model candidate -> confirm base workflow has guardrails -> analyze work patterns -> ask adopter about routing preferences -> create or update `.orchestration/claude-lane.yaml` with routing strategy, model selection criteria, privacy rules, and retention policy -> prefer same-project label routing unless stronger separation is needed -> document routing contract -> use Playwright for visual verification -> apply safe closeout and cleanup rules

## Repo structure

- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/SKILL.md` — main skill definition
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/agents/openai.yaml` — skill discovery and interface metadata
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/references/setup.md` — prerequisites and candidate checks
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/references/routing.md` — routing strategies, model selection criteria, adopter questions
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/references/dispatch.md` — model selection algorithm, queue split, worker lifecycle
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/references/worker-launch.md` — secure Claude worker launch pattern (fetch, worktree, render, launch, finalize, cleanup)
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/references/visual-verification.md` — Playwright-first browser verification guidance
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/references/closeout.md` — outcome blocks, In Review, retries, self-close rules
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/references/troubleshooting.md` — common failure modes
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/references/examples.md` — concrete routing examples across task types
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/assets/claude-lane-profile.example.yaml` — example routing profile with model selection criteria
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/assets/claude-lane-guidance.snippet.md` — starter guidance for adopter repo orchestration docs
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/assets/claude-worker.reference.sh` — reference launcher script (adapt to your environment)
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/assets/worker-prompt.template.md` — worker prompt template with trust boundary, capabilities, and closeout protocol
- `skills/symphony-claude-lane/assets/linear-outcome-block.example.md` — example structured closeout comments

## Install

```bash
npx skills add jvogan/symphony-claude-lane
```

Or copy `skills/symphony-claude-lane/` into your Codex skills directory or reference `SKILL.md` from Claude Code.

## Prerequisites

Requires an existing Symphony + Linear workflow. See [symphony-linear-starter](https://github.com/jvogan/symphony-linear-starter) to set one up.
